meta.title: Senkronla — Sync API & SDK for your app
meta.description: Open-source, self-hosted sync relay — add multi-device sync to your product. SDK guides, REST API reference, and integration checklists.

landing.title: Your users' data, up to date on every device
landing.subtitle: Senkronla is a sync service you plug into your app. Run the relay on your own infrastructure — users can work offline, pick up on another phone or laptop, and you stay in control of the experience without reading their content.

privacy.title: Private by design
privacy.body: Your app sends opaque data packages to the relay. Client-side encryption is used, and recovery phrases never leave the device — only a one-way proof is stored server-side.

offline.title: Works when the network doesn't
offline.body: Changes are saved locally first. When the user comes back online, your app pushes updates and pulls what changed elsewhere.

devices.title: Built for multiple devices
devices.body: Pair a second phone or a desktop app with a short code. You decide how many devices a customer can use and what to charge for extra slots.

landing.howTitle: How it fits into your product

step1.title: Your app saves changes locally
step1.body: Notes, tasks, settings — whatever you sync. The user keeps working even without internet.

step2.title: Senkronla carries versioned snapshots
step2.body: Your integration pushes opaque ENV-RAW1 packages to the sync API. Other devices are notified and pull the latest version.

step3.title: Other devices catch up
step3.body: The SDK or API pulls the latest version. If two people edited at once, your app asks what to keep.

apps.title: Mobile & desktop apps
apps.body: Ship sync without building your own backend team. Focus on features your customers see.

teams.title: Small teams & startups
teams.body: Predictable integration path: SDK first, REST when you need custom flows.

builders.title: Existing SaaS products
builders.body: Add “use on all my devices” to your roadmap with a documented API and error model.

devCta.title: Ready to wire it in?
devCta.body: Follow the guides step by step — most teams complete first sync in under an hour using the SDK.

guides.title: Integration guides
guides.intro: Start here if you are wiring Senkronla into your product for the first time. It is open source and self-hosted — you run the relay on your own servers. We explain every concept in plain language; you do not need to know our codebase beforehand.

concepts.title: Core concepts
concepts.p1: Senkronla syncs one JSON snapshot per customer workspace. These terms appear throughout the SDK and API:
concepts.calloutBody: Your app owns the user experience and data model. Senkronla owns transport: storing opaque packages, versioning, device slots, and notifying other clients.

rows.namespace: A workspace — one isolated sync space, usually one per customer account. Identified by a UUID v4 you choose or generate.
rows.deviceToken: Secret string returned when a device is created or paired. Send as <tag>Bearer</tag> token on every API call. The SDK stores it in <tag>EsrStorage</tag>.
rows.clientDeviceId: UUID generated once on the client and kept forever. Identifies this physical install inside envelopes — different from the server <tag>deviceId</tag> (ULID).
rows.recoveryPhrase: 24-word BIP39 phrase shown once at workspace creation. Proves ownership if all devices are lost. Never sent to the server — only a hash proof.
rows.revision: ULID version tag on each snapshot. Required for optimistic locking on push — mismatch returns <tag>REVISION_CONFLICT</tag>.
rows.envelope: <tag>ESR-DOC1</tag> wrapper around your JSON snapshot plus metadata. The relay stores it but does not parse your app data.
rows.primaryDocument: v1 supports exactly one document per namespace (<tag>documentId: primary</tag>) — typically your full app state as JSON.
rows.pairingCode: Six-digit code valid for a few minutes. Host device generates it; guest device redeems it to join the workspace.

checklist.title: Integration checklist
checklist.p1: Work through this list before shipping to production:

s1.title: Get your relay URL
s1.body: You need a running Senkronla relay. This documentation uses {relayUrl}.

s2.title: Install the SDK
s2.body: Add <tag>@senkronla/client</tag> to your app (or plan REST calls for non-JS clients).

s3.title: Implement DocumentAdapter
s3.body: <tag>exportDocument</tag> / <tag>importDocument</tag> must round-trip your app state as JSON. Keep exports fast — they run before every push.

s4.title: Handle recovery UI
s4.body: <tag>onRecoveryPhrase</tag> fires once. Build a modal with copy/save — you cannot retrieve the phrase later.

s5.title: Handle conflicts
s5.body: <tag>onConflict</tag> must ask the user to keep local or remote. There is no automatic merge.

s6.title: Wire the sync loop
s6.body: <tag>ensureNamespace()</tag> → <tag>sync()</tag> on startup → <tag>notifyLocalChange()</tag> after edits → <tag>flushPush()</tag> before logout.

firstDevice.title: First device in a workspace
firstDevice.p1: This is the path for a brand-new customer who has no synced data yet:
firstDevice.p2: After <tag>ensureNamespace()</tag>, the device token and revision state live in <tag>EsrStorage</tag> — users do not manage tokens manually.

s1.title: Pick a stable namespaceId
s1.body: Use your internal customer/workspace UUID. It must stay the same across app reinstalls if you want the same sync space.

s2.title: Create the adapter
s2.body: Point <tag>exportDocument</tag> at your store snapshot and <tag>importDocument</tag> at your restore logic.

s4.title: Call ensureNamespace()
s4.body: Creates the workspace on first run, shows recovery phrase, performs initial push.

s5.title: Hook local changes
s5.body: Call <tag>notifyLocalChange()</tag> whenever your store mutates. The SDK debounces pushes (default 2 seconds).

secondDevice.title: Add a second device
secondDevice.p1: The guest device needs the same <tag>namespaceId</tag> in its adapter but does not have a token yet.

s1.title: Host calls startPairing()
s1.body: Display the 6-digit code and optional QR (<tag>qrPayload</tag> uses <tag>esr://pair/v1/...</tag>).

s2.title: Guest calls joinPairing(code)
s2.body: Receives a device token, stores it, and runs <tag>sync()</tag> to download data.

s3.title: Verify slot limits
s3.body: If the workspace is full, pairing returns <tag>DEVICE_LIMIT_*</tag>. Surface your upgrade UI via <tag>onDeviceLimit</tag>.

recovery.title: When all devices are lost
recovery.p1: The user enters their 24-word recovery phrase. The SDK builds a cryptographic proof and calls the <tag>recover</tag> endpoint.
recovery.warnBody: Recovery revokes every previously paired device. All other phones and laptops lose access until paired again.

s1.title: Collect the phrase
s1.body: Normalize whitespace; the SDK handles casing.

s2.title: Call sync.recover(phrase)
s2.body: Call <tag>sync.recover(phrase)</tag> — stores a fresh device token for this install.

s3.title: Run sync()
s3.body: Downloads the latest remote snapshot into your adapter via <tag>sync()</tag>.

offline.title: Offline edits and conflicts
offline.p1: Senkronla is offline-friendly by design. The SDK queues local changes and syncs when the network returns.
offline.tipBody: If two devices edit offline and both push, the second push gets <tag>REVISION_CONFLICT</tag>. Your <tag>onConflict</tag> callback decides the winner — plan UI copy accordingly.

s1.title: User edits offline
s1.body: Save locally as usual, then call <tag>notifyLocalChange()</tag>. Status may show <tag>offline</tag> or <tag>pending_push</tag>.

s2.title: Network returns
s2.body: Scheduler or manual <tag>sync()</tag> attempts push/pull automatically.

limits.title: Device limits in your UI
limits.p1: Each workspace has <tag>maxDevices</tag> = free slots + purchased slots. Your product decides what happens when the limit is hit:
limits.li2: <tag>DEVICE_LIMIT_BLOCKED</tag> — hard cap; user must revoke an old device via <tag>listDevices()</tag> + <tag>revokeDevice()</tag>.
limits.li3: Unlock codes from your operator are redeemed with <tag>redeemUnlockCode()</tag>.

choose.title: SDK or REST?
choose.p1: Use the SDK unless you have a strong reason not to — it saves weeks of edge-case handling.
choose.sdkBody: Browser, Electron, React Native (with fetch), Node 18+. Handles tokens, debounce, WS notifications, conflicts.
choose.apiBody: Swift, Kotlin, server jobs, or custom sync engines. You implement revision checks, token storage, and notification polling yourself.

sdk.title: Client SDK reference
sdk.intro: Package: <tag>@senkronla/client</tag>. The <tag>EsrSync</tag> class is your main entry point — it wraps HTTP, optional <tag>WebSocket</tag> notifications, local revision tracking, and user-facing callbacks.

quickStart.title: Quick start
quickStart.p1: Copy this template into your app and replace the store hooks with your real state management:
quickStart.tipBody: Set <tag>relayUrl</tag> to {relayUrl} or read it from your own config.

install.title: Install
install.p1: Requires Node 18+ or a modern browser with fetch and Web Crypto.
install.p2: TypeScript types are included. For manual envelope building, also add <tag>@senkronla/protocol</tag>.

connect.title: EsrSync.connect options
connect.p1: Only <tag>relayUrl</tag>, <tag>document</tag>, <tag>storage</tag>, <tag>onRecoveryPhrase</tag>, and <tag>onConflict</tag> are required. Everything else has sensible defaults:
connect.p2: Use <tag>onStatusChange</tag> to drive a sync indicator in your UI, and <tag>onError</tag> for logging.

options.relayUrl: Base URL ending in <tag>/v1</tag>, e.g. https://sync.example.com/v1
options.onRecoveryPhrase: Required. Called once with the 24-word phrase when namespace is created.
options.onConflict: Required. Return <tag>remote</tag>, <tag>local</tag>, or <tag>cancel</tag> when versions diverge.
options.onDeviceLimit: Optional. Called on <tag>DEVICE_LIMIT_*</tag> errors — open billing UI.
options.notificationsEnabled: Default true. Set false for CLI tools or tests.
options.persistRecoveryPhrase: Default true. Stores phrase in <tag>EsrStorage</tag> (consider security implications).

adapter.title: Document adapter
adapter.p1: The adapter is the bridge between your app state and Senkronla. Use <tag>createDocumentAdapter</tag> for a quick start, or implement <tag>DocumentAdapter</tag> directly:
adapter.p2: <tag>contentType</tag> should be a vendor MIME type. <tag>encryption.enabled</tag> must stay false until <tag>ENV-ENC1</tag> ships.

fields.namespaceId: Stable UUID v4 for this workspace — must match across devices.
fields.namespaceLabel: Human-readable name shown in device lists.
fields.buildDocument: Async. Returns JSON string of current app state.
fields.importDocument: Async. Parses remote JSON string and applies to your store.
fields.contentType: MIME type describing your snapshot format.

storage.title: What the SDK stores locally
storage.p1: Implement <tag>EsrStorage</tag> or use <tag>createLocalStorageAdapter(prefix)</tag>. Keys are scoped per namespace:
storage.li2: <tag>knownRemoteRevision</tag> — last seen server revision for conflict detection
storage.calloutBody: Treat device tokens like session secrets. On mobile, prefer secure storage (Keychain / Keystore) by implementing <tag>EsrStorage</tag> yourself.

methods.title: EsrSync methods
methods.p1: Call these from your app lifecycle hooks:

rows.ensureNamespace: Create workspace on first launch, or verify existing token. Shows recovery phrase when created=true.
rows.sync: Full pull/push cycle. Call on app start, network reconnect, and after WS <tag>head_changed</tag>.
rows.notifyLocalChange: Mark local data dirty; debounced push follows.
rows.flushPush: Push immediately — use before logout or critical saves.
rows.joinPairing: Guest: redeems code, stores token, runs <tag>sync()</tag>.
rows.recover: Recovery phrase flow. Revokes all other devices.
rows.listDevices: Returns devices array and limits for settings UI.
rows.revokeDevice: Remove another device by server deviceId (ULID).
rows.redeemUnlockCode: Apply operator unlock code for more device slots.
rows.resolveConflict: Manual resolution if you handle conflicts outside onConflict.

revokeDevice.desc: Remove another device from the workspace.

sync.title: Sync lifecycle
sync.p1: Typical integration points in your app:

pairing.title: Pairing devices
pairing.p1: Both devices use the same <tag>relayUrl</tag>. The guest adapter must use the same <tag>namespaceId</tag> as the host.

conflicts.title: Handling conflicts
conflicts.p1: A conflict means the server revision advanced while you had unpushed local edits. The SDK pauses and waits for your callback.
conflicts.p2: <tag>remoteMeta</tag> includes <tag>writtenAt</tag>, <tag>deviceId</tag>, and <tag>contentSha256</tag> — enough to show a meaningful choice in UI.

notifications.title: Live notifications
notifications.p1: When enabled, the SDK opens a <tag>WebSocket</tag> to <tag>.../notifications</tag> and listens for <tag>head_changed</tag>.
notifications.p2: If <tag>WebSocket</tag> fails, it falls back to HTTP polling (<tag>ws_with_poll_fallback</tag> mode). WS only notifies — you still pull via HTTP.
notifications.li2: <tag>limits_changed</tag> → slot count updated (handle in <tag>onDeviceLimit</tag> or poll limits)

rows.pendingPush: Local changes queued, waiting for debounce or network

errors.title: Client error codes
errors.p1: All SDK errors are <tag>EsrError</tag> instances with a stable <tag>code</tag> string:
errors.p2: Server-side codes (full list) are on the API page — including relay quotas (default 50 MB envelope, rate limits). Branch on <tag>error.code</tag>, not HTTP status alone.

client.noToken: No device token yet — call <tag>ensureNamespace</tag>, <tag>joinPairing</tag>, or <tag>recover</tag>
client.namespaceExists: Workspace already exists — use pairing or recovery instead of create
client.conflictCancelled: User cancelled conflict dialog — local edits still pending
client.revisionConflict: Server revision moved — conflict flow required
client.deviceLimit: Workspace full — show upgrade or device management UI

api.title: REST API reference
api.intro: JSON over HTTPS under <tag>/v1</tag>. Use this when the JavaScript SDK is not an option, or when you need server-side automation.

overview.title: Overview
overview.p1: All business endpoints are prefixed with <tag>/v1</tag>. Responses are JSON. Errors use a consistent shape with <tag>error.code</tag> you can switch on.
overview.p2: Unauthenticated: <tag>POST /v1/namespaces</tag>, <tag>POST .../devices</tag> (pairing redeem), <tag>POST .../recover</tag>. Everything else needs a device token.
overview.calloutBody: Errors return JSON with an <tag>error</tag> object containing <tag>code</tag>, <tag>message</tag>, and optional <tag>details</tag> (e.g. <tag>remoteMeta</tag> on <tag>REVISION_CONFLICT</tag>).

auth.title: Authentication
auth.p1: After creating, pairing, or recovering a device you receive <tag>deviceToken</tag> in the response. Send it on every subsequent request:
auth.p2: Revoked when the device is deleted or after recovery (all devices revoked). Store securely on the client.
auth.li2: <tag>WebSocket</tag>: same token in <tag>Authorization</tag> header or first auth message

workflows.title: Typical REST flow (no SDK)
workflows.p1: Follow this sequence for a minimal integration:

s2.title: Save deviceToken
s2.body: Persist the token from the <tag>201</tag> response.

s4.title: Push snapshot
s4.body: <tag>PUT .../primary</tag> with envelope. First push: no <tag>expectedRevision</tag>. Updates: must match meta revision.

s5.title: Poll or subscribe
s5.body: <tag>WebSocket head_changed</tag> or periodic <tag>GET head/meta</tag> on other devices.

s6.title: Pull changes
s6.body: <tag>GET .../head</tag> when meta revision differs from local known revision.

namespaces.title: Workspaces (namespaces)
namespaces.p1: One namespace per customer workspace. <tag>namespaceId</tag> must be UUID v4.

documents.title: Documents
documents.p1: v1 syncs a single primary document — your app state as an <tag>ESR-DOC1</tag> envelope.
documents.head: Full envelope for import
documents.p2: Always compare revision before push. Mismatch → <tag>REVISION_CONFLICT</tag> with <tag>remoteMeta</tag> in <tag>details</tag>.
documents.p3: The serialized envelope must fit within the relay's <tag>maxEnvelopeBytes</tag> limit (default <tag>52,428,800 bytes (50 MB)</tag>). Larger payloads return <tag>413 ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE</tag>.

devices.title: Devices & recovery
devices.p1: Pairing and recovery endpoints do not require an existing token (recovery uses phrase proof instead).
devices.revoke: Remove a device (cannot remove last device)
devices.recover: Phrase proof → new token, all other devices revoked
devices.warnBody: <tag>POST .../recover</tag> invalidates every existing device token in the workspace. Plan your UX accordingly.

limits.title: Limits & unlock
limits.unlock: Redeem unlock code for more slots

websocket.title: WebSocket notifications
websocket.p1: Connect to the notifications URL with the device token. Subprotocol: <tag>esr-notifications-v1</tag>.
websocket.p2: Messages are notifications only — always fetch document data via HTTP <tag>GET</tag>.
websocket.li1: <tag>head_changed</tag> — new revision available, pull when convenient

relayQuotas.title: Relay quotas & size limits
relayQuotas.p1: The relay operator configures these in <tag>config.yaml</tag> or <tag>ESR_*</tag> environment variables. If nothing is set, the defaults below apply automatically — limits are on by default.
relayQuotas.sizeBody: Measured on the full serialized <tag>ESR-DOC1</tag> JSON at push time. Default: <tag>52,428,800 bytes (50 MB)</tag>. Configure with <tag>sync.maxEnvelopeBytes</tag> or <tag>ESR_MAX_ENVELOPE_BYTES</tag>.
relayQuotas.rateP1: Sliding-window counters in PostgreSQL. Exempt from the general IP quota: <tag>/health</tag>, <tag>/metrics</tag>, and WebSocket <tag>.../notifications</tag>.
relayQuotas.responseP1: Successful responses include <tag>RateLimit-Limit</tag>, <tag>RateLimit-Remaining</tag>, and <tag>RateLimit-Reset</tag> headers (seconds until the window resets). Push also sends <tag>RateLimit-Push-*</tag>. Pull and push JSON bodies may include a <tag>rateLimits</tag> object keyed by action.
relayQuotas.responseP2: On <tag>429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED</tag>, use <tag>Retry-After</tag> and <tag>error.details.rateLimit</tag> for backoff.

rows.token: Re-pair or recover — token invalid or revoked
rows.noDocument: No push yet — expected on first pull
rows.exists: Namespace taken — pair or recover instead
rows.tooLarge: Envelope exceeds <tag>maxEnvelopeBytes</tag> (default 50 MB) — shrink snapshot or ask operator to raise limit
rows.rateLimit: Quota exceeded — backoff using <tag>Retry-After</tag> and <tag>RateLimit-*</tag> headers
rows.pairing: Code expired or wrong — generate a new one

operator.title: Operator console
operator.intro: Relay administration — namespaces, unlock codes, and activity logs.
operator.loginIntro: Sign in with your relay admin token to access operator tools.
operator.loginFailed: Invalid admin token or admin API is disabled.
operator.loadFailed: Failed to load data from the relay.
operator.unlockHint: Create a redeemable code for extra device slots on a namespace.
operator.adminTokenHint: Same value as ESR_ADMIN_TOKEN in your relay config
operator.requestFailed: Request failed. Check the namespace ID and that the API is running.
